To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) attention visualizations should be treated with caution when explaining deep learning models, (2) attention visualizations are not a good proxy for word importance, (3) self-attention based models are not interpretable, (4) attention visualizations do not provide any information about the underlying model.
the attention maps in the Transformer are not over words, but over mixed embeddings, and that this mixing is already significant after the first layer, making attention visualizations misleading.
the attention maps of the Transformer and BERT do not provide valid explanations of the models' decisions and that the attention maps are highly misleading.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the attention mechanism in Transformer models is a valid explanation for the predictions of these models.
the validity of self attention as a valid explanation for transformer models.
the question of whether self attention based models are indeed explainable by just looking at attention maps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self attention mechanism in Transformer based models is not valid as an explanation for the output of the model.
attention visualizations can be misleading, but they can be helpful in some situations.
self attention is not a valid method of explanation for Transformer models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-attention based Transformer models are not explainable by the attention maps.
the attention is over mixed embeddings, which is why the attention maps are not as interpretable as often thought.

attention is not the right explanation for Transformer models and we should look into other explanations.
